decisions.reason: As a close extension of the firm's established portfolio, the vertigo combination tablet fits its formulation strengths and is likely worth backing beyond its first launch year.

The generic antidepressant is comparatively far from the firm's established focus and is likely to face intense price and reimbursement pressure, so management would redeploy resources to better-fitting differentiated products and services.

The combination antihypertensive tablet is close to the core prescription business and supports the firm's strategy of growing improved formulations within its existing manufacturing and regulatory capabilities.
The bone and joint supplement supports the stated aim to expand differentiated self-care and pharmacy-oriented products that reduce dependence on reimbursement-driven prescription markets.
